enriched.title: Platão, Vocabulário e Conceitos Filosóficos em Inglês
enriched.summary: A aula explora o pensamento de Platão sobre o mundo físico e o mundo das ideias, enfatizando conceitos filosóficos, vocabulário relacionado e estrutura gramatical. Além disso, há um vídeo sobre a importância do céu noturno para a sobrevivência humana.

vocabulary.definition: An observable event or occurrence, especially one that is unusual or remarkable.
examples: A rainbow is a natural phenomenon.
The Northern Lights are an incredible phenomenon.

vocabulary.definition: Plural of phenomenon, meaning multiple observable events or occurrences.
examples: Scientists study natural phenomena to understand the world.
Social phenomena are complex and diverse.

vocabulary.definition: To age or become older over time.
examples: We all grow old eventually.
Trees grow old and sometimes rot.

vocabulary.definition: The quality or state of being true or factual.
examples: The truth is often hard to accept.
Honesty is important to tell the truth.

vocabulary.definition: In accordance with fact or reality.
examples: Her story was true.
It’s true that the sun rises in the east.

vocabulary.definition: A period of history that happened a very long time ago.
examples: In ancient times, people relied on the stars for navigation.
Ancient times were marked by the rise of civilizations.

vocabulary.definition: To emphasize or make something stand out.
examples: The teacher highlighted the key points in the text.
This report highlights the importance of education.

vocabulary.definition: The practice of cultivating land and raising crops and livestock.
examples: Agriculture was crucial in ancient times.
Modern agriculture relies on technology.

vocabulary.definition: To calculate or determine the passage of time.
examples: People used the sun to measure time in the past.
Clocks are used to measure time accurately.
The lecture was very interesting.
She shared an interesting idea.

grammar.explanation: Some nouns have irregular plural forms, such as phenomenon (singular) and phenomena (plural).
rules: Singular nouns refer to one object or idea.
Plural nouns refer to more than one object or idea and may have irregular forms.
examples: phenomenon → phenomena
child → children
commonMistakes: Using 'phenomenons' instead of 'phenomena' as the plural of 'phenomenon'.

expressions.meaning: To age or become older over time.
expressions.usage: Commonly used to talk about the passage of time or aging.
examples: We all grow old eventually.
Trees grow old and sometimes rot.

practiceQuestions.question: What is the plural of 'phenomenon'?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The plural of 'phenomenon' is 'phenomena', as it follows an irregular pattern.

practiceQuestions.question: Translate: 'Physical objects grow old, change, and disappear.'
practiceQuestions.answer: Os objetos físicos envelhecem, mudam e desaparecem.
practiceQuestions.explanation: This is a direct translation of the sentence.

culturalNotes: Platão foi um filósofo grego que influenciou profundamente o pensamento ocidental.
Na antiguidade, as pessoas mediam o tempo observando o sol e as estrelas.
studyTips: Pratique a pronúncia das palavras difíceis repetindo-as várias vezes.
Compare as ideias de Platão com exemplos do mundo moderno para fixar os conceitos.
originalExamples: The real world is only an imperfect copy of the world of ideas. (O mundo real é apenas uma cópia imperfeita do mundo das ideias.)
Physical objects grow old, change, and disappear. (Os objetos físicos envelhecem, mudam e desaparecem.)
Perfect ideas never change. (As ideias perfeitas nunca mudam.)
For example, all chairs are different, but there is a perfect idea of a chair. (Por exemplo, todas as cadeiras são diferentes, mas existe uma ideia perfeita de 'cadeira'.)
Plato believed that true knowledge comes from the world of ideas. (Platão acreditava que o verdadeiro conhecimento vem do mundo das ideias.)
Our senses can deceive us. (Nossos sentidos podem nos enganar.)
The human mind tries to find the truth behind appearances. (A mente humana tenta encontrar a verdade por trás das aparências.)
The Philosopher tries to understand the essence of perfect ideas. (O filósofo procura compreender as ideias perfeitas.)
According to Plato, the ideas are eternal. (Segundo Platão, as ideias são eternas.)
The World of ideas can’t be seen by our eyes. (O mundo das ideias não pode ser visto com os olhos.)
According to Plato, the reality is split into two worlds: The physical world and the world of ideas. (Segundo Platão, a realidade é dividida em dois mundos: o mundo físico e o mundo das ideias.)
